CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFFORM

CFFORM writes an HTML FORM tag and collects the validation rules of the CFINPUT, CFSELECT, CFTEXTINPUT and CFTREE controls inside it into a JavaScript function that runs when the user submits the form. It is also the required container for the Java-style controls CFGRID, CFTREE, CFSLIDER, CFTEXTINPUT and CFAPPLET.

Category

Forms

Syntax

<CFFORM NAME="name"
    ACTION="form_action"
    METHOD="POST"
    TARGET="window_name"
    ENCTYPE="type"
    ONSUBMIT="javascript"
    PRESERVEDATA="Yes/No"
    ENABLECAB="Yes/No"
    PASSTHROUGH="HTML_attributes">
  form controls
</CFFORM>

Attributes

NAME
Optional. Form name, used in the generated JavaScript. KoldFusion names unnamed forms CFForm_1, CFForm_2...
ACTION
Optional. Page that processes the form. Defaults to the current page.
METHOD
Optional, default "POST". POST or GET.
TARGET
Optional. Window or frame that receives the response.
ENCTYPE
Optional. Encoding type, for example "multipart/form-data" for file uploads with CFFILE.
ONSUBMIT
Optional. JavaScript statement inserted into the generated check function, after the validation checks; for example return confirm('Send it?');.
PRESERVEDATA
Optional, default "No". Yes fills the controls with the values submitted to this page instead of their VALUE / SELECTED defaults. Works for text fields, CFTEXTINPUT and CFSELECT.
ENABLECAB
Optional. Offered Internet Explorer users the applet classes as a .cab download. Accepted for compatibility; KoldFusion ignores it.
PASSTHROUGH
Optional. Extra HTML attributes copied into the FORM tag as they are.

Usage

CFFORM emits a reference to /CFIDE/scripts/cfform.js (the validation library), a function _CF_checkformname that tests each rule in turn, and a FORM tag whose onSubmit calls it. When a check fails, the user sees the control's MESSAGE in an alert box and the field gets the focus. Plain HTML controls may be mixed freely with the CF ones.

Validation runs in the browser, so a user with JavaScript turned off skips it. For server-side checks use hidden fields such as fieldname_required in an ordinary form, or validate in the action page.

With PRESERVEDATA, radio buttons and check boxes keep their own VALUE and are CHECKED when it matches what was submitted.

In 1999 the grid, tree, slider and text input controls were Java applets. Browsers dropped Java long ago, so KoldFusion renders working HTML versions styled after the applets.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFIF IsDefined("Form.FieldNames")>
  <H3>You sent:</H3>
  <UL>
  <CFLOOP LIST="#Form.FieldNames#" INDEX="Field">
    <CFOUTPUT><LI>#Field# = #HTMLEditFormat(Evaluate("Form." & Field))#</CFOUTPUT>
  </CFLOOP>
  </UL>
</CFIF>

<CFFORM NAME="Signup" ACTION="cfform.cfm">
<TABLE>
<TR><TD>Name:</TD>
  <TD><CFINPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="FullName" SIZE="25" REQUIRED="Yes"
      MESSAGE="Please tell us your name."></TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Year of birth:</TD>
  <TD><CFINPUT TYPE="Text" NAME="BirthYear" SIZE="4" VALIDATE="integer"
      RANGE="1900,1999" MESSAGE="A year between 1900 and 1999, please."></TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Connection:</TD>
  <TD><CFSELECT NAME="Modem">
      <OPTION>28.8K modem<OPTION SELECTED>56K modem<OPTION>ISDN<OPTION>T1 at work
      </CFSELECT></TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<INPUT TYPE="Submit" VALUE="Sign me up">
</CFFORM>
